questions.stem: What is the formal charge on sulfur in the SO2 structure with one S=O double bond, one S-O single bond and one lone pair on S?
questions.explanation: Sulfur has 6 valence electrons, 2 nonbonding electrons (one lone pair) and 3 bonds (one double and one single). The formal charge is 6 - 2 - 3 = +1. Zero would need 4 bonds with the same lone pair. A charge of -1 or +2 does not match the electron count of this structure.

questions.stem: In which compound is the C-H bond most acidic?
questions.explanation: The sp carbon of propyne has 50 percent s character, stabilizing the conjugate base (pKa about 25). Propene's sp2 C-H (about 44) and the alkane C-H bonds (about 50) are far less acidic.

questions.stem: Which compound has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Octane is linear and has the most electrons and surface area, so its London forces are strongest. Hexane and propane are smaller. 2,2,3,3-Tetramethylbutane is a compact, branched C8 isomer that has less surface contact and boils lower than octane.

questions.stem: How many stereocenters are in the open-chain form of glucose, an aldohexose (CHO-CHOH-CHOH-CHOH-CHOH-CH2OH)?
questions.explanation: C2 to C5 each carry four different groups, while C1 (CHO) and C6 (CH2OH) are not stereocenters. That is four stereocenters and 2^4 = 16 aldohexose stereoisomers.
It has two stereocenters with identical ends, so the (R,S) form is meso. The stereoisomers are (R,R), (S,S) and meso, giving three rather than four.

demo_cards.front: How do you calculate the formal charge of an atom in a Lewis structure?
demo_cards.back: Formal charge = valence electrons minus nonbonding electrons minus the number of bonds (half the bonding electrons).

demo_cards.text: Formal charge = {{c1::valence electrons}} minus {{c2::nonbonding electrons}} minus {{c3::number of bonds}}.
demo_cards.extra: Each lone pair counts as 2 nonbonding electrons; each bond counts as 1.

demo_cards.stem: Formal charge on nitrogen in NH4+ (four N-H bonds, no lone pair)?
demo_cards.why: 5 - 0 - 4 = +1. N normally makes three bonds, so a fourth bond means a positive formal charge.

demo_cards.statement: The formal charges in a Lewis structure sum to the overall charge of the molecule or ion.
demo_cards.why: Zero for a neutral molecule, and equal to the ionic charge for an ion.
